task.title: Mount and search one tree at a time
task.problem: All source trees are mounted before searching, although rg now runs sequentially per tree. Peak mounts and resident daemon/process costs grow with unique trees.
task.proposal: Prioritize mount lifetimes after BSG-010 reproduces the reviewer baseline. Start with mount/search/cleanup scoped to one tree; compare a configurable small bounded pool, preserving resource ownership and output semantics. Reviewer measurements suggest serial mount startup (~52 ms/tree) dominates rg startup (~5 ms/tree), but pool speedups remain unmeasured. The reported mount stage includes a 50 ms readiness-poll interval in ensure_mount; measure that overhead and compare an adaptive shorter initial poll before attributing the whole stage to actual mount startup or adding a pool.
acceptance: Peak active owned mounts is one in serial mode.
All element mappings, origins, partial-error statuses and interruption cleanup are preserved.
Measure many-tree latency/RSS and identify any regressions against BSG-010.
For any pool, active owned mounts/processes never exceed the configured bound and cancellation/error cleanup covers every worker.
evidence: Each unique tree is mounted, searched and released before the next; --stats reports peak mounts 1, one buildbox-fuse and one rg process per tree.
Readiness polling backs off from 1 ms to 50 ms; release stops buildbox-fuse with SIGTERM (it unmounts itself) and falls back to fusermount/umount only if the mount survives.

content-unique-trees (300 trees): wall 19.97 s -> 5.14 s, mount 15.43 s -> 1.34 s, cleanup 1.54 s -> 0.56 s, peak mounts 300 -> 1; other scenarios unchanged or faster (content-small-files 1.86 -> 1.73 s).
Bounded pool deferred to BSG-021: measured gain is real (~2.5 s on 300 trees) but needs ordered, streaming output and pooled cancellation cleanup.
